xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Additional Commissioner Of Customs, Noida Customs Commissionerate
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs:
The Company vide its Letter dated 9th April,2024 has informed about receipt of an Order from Additional Commissioner, Noida Customs Commissionerate, Uttar Pradesh, dated 22nd March, 2024 (received on 9th April, 2024) demanding an amount of Rs. 33.43 Crore as duty short paid along with applicable interest and imposing penalty of Rs. 82 Crore under the Customs Act, 1962. In the same order, redemption fine of Rs.191.76 Crore was also imposed on the goods already cleared during the period from 1st July 2017 to 1st February 2021.
Thereafter, an appeal against the said order was filed on7th June 2024, before the Commissioner of Customs (Appeals), GST Bhawan, Sector-48, Noida.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, E-Block, Nehru Colony, Haridwar Road, Dehradun, Uttarakhand.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The matter pertains to the classification of “RAB” under the Central Excise Tariff Act 1985 for the financial years 2005–2009. The Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise, by an order dated 9th May 2019, had raised a demand of Rs.10,39,32,564 along with applicable interest and penalty. This order was subsequently set aside by the Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), New Delhi, in favour of the Company. Aggrieved by the CESTAT order, Commissioner of CGST & Central Excise has filed an appeal before the Hon’ble High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital. As the Company did not receive any notice from the Hon’ble High Court in this matter but was informed by its consultant after the case appeared on the Court’s website. Consequently, the requisite disclosure was made on July 21, 2025. Thereafter, during the quarter ended September 30, 2025, the Company appeared before the Hon’ble High Court.
